p.src: At that moment, Wu the Scholar said to Song Gongming, “There is only one way to break this sorcery: send someone quickly to Jizhou to find Gongsun Sheng. He will be able to defeat it.” Song Jiang said, “Dai Zong went there before and searched for quite some time without learning anything at all. Where are we to find him?” Wu Yong said, “Jizhou governs a great many counties, towns, markets, and villages. He surely cannot have searched them all. Gongsun Sheng, I think, is a man of lofty and unworldly character, and must be dwelling in some famed mountain or grotto, beside some great river or in some hallowed retreat. This time, have Dai Zong make the circuit of the famous mountains and immortal retreats in the counties under Jizhou and search them thoroughly. Then there is no fear he will fail to find him.” When Song Jiang had heard him out, he immediately summoned Warden Dai to discuss going to Jizhou in search of Gongsun Sheng. Dai Zong said, “I am willing to go, but I should like someone to accompany me.” Wu Yong said, “Once you employ your Magic Traveling Method, who could possibly keep up with you?” Dai Zong said, “If I have a companion, I can fasten spirit-horse talismans to his legs as well and enable him to cover just as many miles.” Li Kui promptly said, “I will go with Warden Dai.” Dai Zong said, “If you wish to come with me, you must eat no meat throughout the journey and obey everything I say.” Li Kui said, “What is so difficult about that? I will do everything you say.” Song Jiang and Wu Yong instructed them, “Take great care on the road and do not stir up trouble. If you find him, return as soon as you can.” Li Kui said, “I killed Yin Tianxi and landed Master Chai in a criminal case. How could I not want to save him? This time I certainly will not cause any trouble.” The two men concealed their weapons, tied up their bundles, and took leave of Song Jiang and the others. Departing Gaotangzhou, they set out along the road to Jizhou.

p.src: After they had gone a little over twenty li, Li Kui stopped and said, “Brother, let us buy a bowl of wine before we go on.” Dai Zong said, “If you are to accompany me under the Magic Traveling Method, you must drink only meatless wine. For now, let us press on.” Li Kui replied, “What does it matter if I eat a little meat?” Dai Zong said, “There you go again. It is already late today. Let us find an inn for the night and leave early tomorrow.” The two went another thirty-odd li. When darkness fell, they found an inn and stopped there. A fire was lit and rice cooked, and they bought a measure of wine to drink. Li Kui carried a bowl of meatless rice and a bowl of vegetable soup into their room for Dai Zong to eat. Dai Zong asked, “Why are you not eating?” Li Kui answered, “I do not want any rice just yet.” Dai Zong thought, “That rogue is surely hiding from me to eat meat behind my back.” Dai Zong finished his own meatless meal, then quietly went to look behind the inn. There he saw Li Kui consuming two measures of wine and a plate of beef by himself. Dai Zong thought, “Just as I said! I shall say nothing to him now and play a little trick on him tomorrow.” Dai Zong returned to the room and went to sleep. After Li Kui had eaten and drunk for a while, he feared Dai Zong might rebuke him, so he quietly returned to the room and went to bed.

p.src: At the fifth watch, Dai Zong rose and told Li Kui to light the fire. They cooked and ate some meatless rice, divided the baggage between them, settled their lodging bill, and left the inn. Before they had gone two li, Dai Zong said, “We did not use the Magic Traveling Method yesterday, so today we must make up the distance. First tie your bundle securely. I shall work the spell upon you, and we will stop after traveling eight hundred li.” Dai Zong took four spirit-horse talismans and fastened them to Li Kui’s legs, instructing him, “Wait for me at an eating and drinking shop ahead.” Dai Zong murmured his incantation and blew a breath upon Li Kui’s legs. Li Kui opened his stride and sped away as though riding the clouds, swift as flight. Dai Zong laughed and said, “Let him endure hunger for a day.” Dai Zong then fastened spirit-horse talismans to himself and hurried after him. Li Kui did not understand the method and supposed it would be no different from traveling with Dai Zong in the ordinary way. All he heard was the roar of wind and rain beside his ears; the houses and trees on both sides seemed to topple in unbroken ranks, while beneath his feet it was as though clouds drove him and mist urged him onward. Li Kui grew frightened and tried several times to stop, but could not bring his legs under control. It seemed as though someone were pushing him from below; his feet scarcely touched the ground, and he kept running onward. Though he saw taverns and eating houses, he could not enter them to buy food. Li Kui could only cry, “Good master, stop a moment!” By the time the red sun neared the western horizon, his belly was both hungry and thirsty, yet he was less able than ever to stop. He was so terrified that foul sweat covered his body, and he gasped for breath. Dai Zong caught up from behind and called, “Brother Li, why did you not buy yourself some refreshments before going on?” Li Kui answered, “Brother, save me! Iron Ox is starving to death!” Dai Zong took several steamed flatbreads from inside his robe and began eating them himself. Li Kui cried, “I cannot stop to buy food. Give me two of those to stay my hunger.” Dai Zong said, “Brother, catch up with me and I will give you some.” Li Kui stretched out his hand, but a distance of about one zhang always remained between them, and he could not reach the food. Li Kui cried, “Good brother, wait for me!” Dai Zong said, “There is indeed something strange today. I cannot stop my own two legs either.” Li Kui said, “Ah! These damned legs of mine will not obey me in the slightest and just keep running like this. I may as well use my great axe to hack off the lower halves!” Dai Zong said, “That is indeed the only thing to do. Otherwise, even if you run until New Year’s Day next year, you still will not stop.” Li Kui said, “Good brother, do not use your arts to make sport of me. If I cut off my legs, you will only laugh at me.” Dai Zong said, “Could it be that you disobeyed me last night? Today even I cannot stop running. You may go on by yourself.” Li Kui cried, “Good master, have mercy and let me stop for a moment!” Dai Zong said, “My method permits no meat to be eaten, and beef is forbidden above all else. If you have eaten so much as one piece of beef, you must run a full hundred thousand li before you can stop.” Li Kui said, “What misery! Last night I should not have hidden it from you, brother. The truth is, I secretly bought and ate several jin of beef. What am I to do now?” Dai Zong said, “No wonder even my legs will not stop today. We shall simply have to make a journey to the ends of the earth. Taking it slowly, it will be three or five years before we can return.” When Li Kui heard this, he raised a tremendous cry of injustice to heaven. Dai Zong laughed and said, “If from now on you will obey me in one matter, I can bring this spell to an end.” Li Kui said, “My good father, from now on I will do everything you say.” Dai Zong said, “Will you ever dare hide from me and eat meat again?” Li Kui said, “If I ever eat meat again, may a boil as large as a bowl grow upon my tongue!”

p.src: The next day they entered the city, Dai Zong disguised as the master and Li Kui as his servant. They searched throughout the city all day, but found no one who knew Gongsun Sheng, so they returned to the inn to rest. The following day they searched the city’s little streets and narrow alleys for another full day, but learned absolutely nothing. Growing impatient, Li Kui cursed, “Where the devil has that beggar of a Daoist hidden himself? When I see him, I will seize him by the scruff and drag him off to meet our brother.” Dai Zong said, “There you go again. If you do not heed my words, I shall make you suffer once more.” Li Kui laughed and said, “I was only joking.” Dai Zong reproached him for a while longer, and Li Kui dared not answer back. The two returned to the inn and rested again.

p.src: Early the next morning, they went to search the nearby villages, towns, and markets outside the city. Whenever Dai Zong saw an elderly person, he saluted respectfully and asked where Master Gongsun Sheng lived, but not one of them knew him. Dai Zong asked at scores of places. Around noon that day, the two grew hungry from walking. Seeing a vegetarian noodle shop beside the road, they went straight in to buy something to eat. They found every seat inside occupied, with not a single place free, so Dai Zong and Li Kui stood in the aisle. A waiter said, “If you gentlemen wish to eat noodles, share a table with this old man.” Dai Zong saw an elderly gentleman occupying a large table by himself. He saluted him courteously, and the two sat opposite him. Li Kui sat below Dai Zong and ordered the waiter to prepare four large bowls of noodles. Dai Zong said, “I shall eat one, and you three. Will that not be enough?” Li Kui said, “That will not do. Make it six at once; I shall take care of them all.” The waiter laughed when he heard this. They waited a long while, but no noodles came. Li Kui saw the bowls being carried farther inside, and was already half consumed with impatience. Then the waiter brought out a bowl of hot noodles and set it before the old man sharing their table. The old man made no polite demur, but picked up the noodles and began to eat. The noodles were hot, so the old man bent his head low over the table as he ate. Impatient by nature, Li Kui saw that their noodles still had not come and shouted, “Waiter!” He cursed, “You have kept your lord waiting all this time!” He struck the table with his palm, splashing the old man’s face with hot broth and overturning his entire bowl of noodles. The old man flew into a rage, seized Li Kui, and shouted, “What is the meaning of this? Why did you overturn my noodles?” Li Kui raised his fist to strike the old man. Dai Zong hastily shouted for him to stop and apologized: “Good sir, do not lower yourself to his level. I shall pay for another bowl of noodles for you.” The old man said, “You do not understand, sir. I have a long way to go and wanted to finish my noodles early so I could return to hear a sermon. If I am late, it will delay my journey.” Dai Zong asked, “Where are you from, good sir? And whose sermon are you going to hear, and on what subject?” The old man replied, “I am from the foot of Mount Erxian in Jiugong County, which lies under the jurisdiction of Jizhou. I came into the city to buy some fine incense, and am returning to hear Perfected Master Luo expound the method of immortality upon the mountain.” Dai Zong thought, “Could Gongsun Sheng be there as well?” He asked the old man, “Good sir, has there ever been a man named Gongsun Sheng in your village?” The old man said, “If you asked anyone else, they certainly would not know. Many people do not recognize him. I am his neighbor. He has only an aged mother at home. That gentleman long wandered abroad, but now he is known as Gongsun Yiqing. Now that he has forsaken his family name, everyone calls him Daoist Qing, not Gongsun Sheng. That is his secular name, so no one recognizes it.” Dai Zong said, “Truly, ‘One wears out iron shoes searching in vain, then finds it without the slightest effort.’” Dai Zong saluted the old man again and asked, “How far is Mount Erxian in Jiugong County from here? Is Daoist Qing at home?” The old man said, “Mount Erxian is only forty-five li from the county seat. Daoist Qing is Perfected Master Luo’s foremost disciple, and his master will not let him leave his side.” Dai Zong was overjoyed to hear this. He hurried the waiter to bring the noodles. After he, Li Kui, and the old man had eaten together, he settled the bill. They left the shop together, and Dai Zong asked the way. Dai Zong said, “Please go on ahead, good sir. I shall buy some incense and spirit paper and follow shortly.” The old man took his leave and departed.

p.src: Dai Zong came forward and shouted, “Iron Ox! How could you frighten this aged mother into a faint?” Dai Zong hurriedly helped her up. Li Kui threw down his great axe, bowed, and said, “Brother, do not blame me. If I had not done this, you would never have come out.” Gongsun Sheng first helped his mother inside, then came back out and respectfully invited Dai Zong and Li Kui into a clean chamber. Once they were seated, he said, “I am amazed that you two managed to find this place.” Dai Zong said, “After you left the mountain, Master, I first searched all through Jizhou, but could learn nothing of your whereabouts; I succeeded only in gathering a band of brothers and bringing them up to the mountain. Now our elder brother Song Gongming went to Gaotangzhou to rescue Lord Chai, only to be defeated in two or three engagements by the prefect Gao Lian’s sorcery. At our wits’ end, he ordered Li Kui and me to seek you out and invite you back. We searched all over Jizhou but found no trace of you. By chance, at a noodle shop, an old gentleman of these parts directed us here. Then a country girl told us that you were at home refining elixirs, while your aged mother persisted in denying it. That was why I had Li Kui provoke you into coming out, Master. The fellow was rather too reckless; I beg you to forgive his offense. Our brother is at the Gaotangzhou border, where each day seems a year. Please set out at once, Master, and thus bring the great cause of brotherhood to a noble completion from beginning to end.” Gongsun Sheng said, “In my youth, this poor Daoist wandered the rivers and lakes and often associated with brave men. Since parting from you at Liangshan Marsh and returning home, it is not that I have forgotten my obligations. First, my mother is old and has no one to attend her; second, my true master, the Perfected Luo, detained me before his dwelling. Fearing that someone might come searching for me, I changed my name to the Daoist Qing and concealed myself here.” Dai Zong said, “Song Gongming is now in mortal danger. Out of compassion, Master, you must make this journey.” Gongsun Sheng said, “The difficulty is that there will be no one to support my aged mother, and how could my true master, the Perfected Luo, consent to release me? I truly cannot go.” Dai Zong bowed again and pleaded earnestly. Gongsun Sheng helped him up and said, “Allow me to consider the matter further.” Gongsun Sheng kept Dai Zong and Li Kui seated in the clean chamber and had vegetarian wine and food prepared for them.

p.src: Li Kui felt for his two broad axes, quietly opened the door, and under the bright stars and moon felt his way step by step up the mountain. When he reached the Temple of Purple Emptiness, he found its two great gates shut, but the wattle wall beside them did not seem very high. Li Kui sprang over it, opened the main gates, and crept step by step inside. When he reached the Pine-and-Crane Studio, he heard someone beyond the window chanting the Precious Scripture of the Jade Pivot. Li Kui climbed up and licked a hole through the window paper. Looking inside, he saw Perfected Luo sitting alone upon the cloud couch. On the table before him burned a censer of fine incense and two painted candles, while he chanted the scripture in a clear, ringing voice. Li Kui said, “This thieving priest is surely marked for death!” He slipped around to the doorway and gave it a single push; with a creak, both latticed doors flew open. Li Kui charged inside, raised his axe, and brought it down upon the crown of Perfected Luo’s head. The Perfected One toppled onto the cloud couch, and white blood flowed out. Seeing it, Li Kui laughed. “Plainly this thieving priest has preserved the body of a virgin, nurturing his primal yang without ever spilling it; that is why there is not the least trace of red.” When Li Kui looked more closely, he saw that even the Daoist cap had been split in two, and the head cleaved straight down to the neck. Li Kui said, “Now I have rid the world of a scourge. No need to worry that Gongsun Sheng will refuse to go.” He turned and left the Pine-and-Crane Studio, then dashed out along the side gallery. p.src: Then Perfected Master Luo said, “How would you like me to have the three of you in Gaotangzhou within moments?” The three thanked him. Dai Zong thought, “This Perfected Master Luo is even more powerful than my Divine Traveling Art. …” The Perfected Master called for an acolyte to bring three handkerchiefs. Dai Zong said, “May I ask my master how you will enable us to reach Gaotangzhou at once?” Perfected Master Luo rose and said, “All of you, follow me.” The three followed him out through the abbey gate and onto a rocky ledge. First he took a red handkerchief, spread it on the rock, and said, “My disciple may step onto it.” Gongsun Sheng placed both feet upon it. Perfected Master Luo swept his sleeve and cried, “Rise!” The handkerchief turned into a red cloud, bearing Gongsun Sheng gently upward until he floated more than twenty fathoms above the mountain. Perfected Master Luo cried, “Stop!” The red cloud hung motionless. He next spread out a blue-green handkerchief, told Dai Zong to step onto it, and cried, “Rise!” That handkerchief turned into a blue-green cloud, bore Dai Zong aloft, and rose into the sky. The red and blue-green clouds, each as large as a reed mat, wheeled in the sky, leaving Li Kui dumbfounded. Perfected Master Luo then spread a white handkerchief upon the rock and told Li Kui to step onto it. Li Kui laughed. “You had better not be playing tricks. If I fall, I will raise a mighty great lump!” Perfected Master Luo said, “Can you not see the other two?” Li Kui stood upon the handkerchief, and Perfected Master Luo said, “Rise!” The handkerchief became a white cloud and flew upward. Li Kui cried, “Ai-ya! Mine is unsteady! Let me down!” Perfected Master Luo beckoned with his right hand, and the blue-green and red clouds descended smoothly. Dai Zong bowed his thanks and stood waiting before him, while Gongsun Sheng stood to his left. From above Li Kui shouted, “I need to piss and shit too! If you do not let me down, I will let it all fall right on your head!” Perfected Master Luo asked, “We are men who have left the world and have never offended you. Why did you climb over the wall last night, break in, and hew at me with an axe? Had I possessed no virtue of the Way, I would already have been killed. And you also killed one of my acolytes.” Li Kui said, “It was not me. Surely you have mistaken me for someone else?” Perfected Master Luo laughed. “Though all you hewed apart were two gourds of mine, your heart was wicked. I shall let you suffer a little hardship.” He waved his hand and cried, “Go!” A fierce gust blew Li Kui up among the clouds. Two Yellow-Turbaned Mighty Ones appeared and escorted Li Kui away. With nothing but the roar of wind and rain in his ears, he soon found himself within the borders of Jizhou, so terrified that his soul nearly left his body and his limbs trembled. Suddenly there came a tremendous crash, and he tumbled from the roof of the Jizhou prefectural hall.

p.src: That day Prefect Ma Shihong happened to be holding court. Many clerks and attendants stood before the hall, and all were startled to see a big black fellow fall from the sky. Prefect Ma saw him and shouted, “Seize that rogue and bring him here!” At once more than a dozen jailers and prison guards drove Li Kui before him. Prefect Ma thundered, “What manner of demon are you, rogue? How did you come dropping down from midair?” Li Kui had split his scalp and forehead in the fall and could not speak for a long while. Prefect Ma said, “He must be a demon. Go fetch some implements for subduing sorcery.” The jailers and warders bound Li Kui and threw him onto the grass before the hall. An attendant carried over a basin of dog’s blood and drenched him from head to foot; another brought a bucket of urine and excrement and poured it over Li Kui from his head all the way to his feet. Li Kui had urine and filth in his mouth and ears. Li Kui shouted, “I am no demon! I am an attendant of Perfected Master Luo.” Now everyone in Jizhou knew Perfected Master Luo to be a living immortal in this world, so they dared not harm Li Kui. They brought Li Kui before the hall again, and a clerk promptly reported, “Perfected Master Luo of Jizhou is a living immortal who has attained the Way and is renowned throughout the realm. If this man is his follower, he must not be tortured.” Prefect Ma laughed. “I have read a thousand scrolls and heard of countless events past and present, yet never have I seen an immortal with such a disciple. He is certainly a demon. Jailers, put your backs into beating that rogue!” The men had no choice but to throw Li Kui down and beat him until he saw one Buddha born and another enter nirvana. Prefect Ma shouted, “Confess at once that you are a demon, rogue, and we will stop beating you!” Li Kui had no choice but to confess that he was “Li the Second, the demon.” They clamped a great cangue onto him and escorted him down to the main prison. Upon reaching death row, Li Kui said, “I am the Divine General on Duty. How dare you put me in a cangue? One way or another, I will see that everyone in the city of Jizhou dies!” The chief warder and guards all knew of Perfected Master Luo’s lofty virtue, and there was not one among them who did not revere him. They came to ask Li Kui, “Who exactly are you?” Li Kui said, “I am Perfected Master Luo’s personal attendant, the Divine General on Duty. Because I made a momentary mistake and angered the Perfected Master, he cast me down here to endure this suffering. In two or three days he will surely come for me. If you do not bring me wine and food to restore my strength, I shall have every member of all your families killed.” Hearing him speak this way, the chief warder and jailers all became afraid and had no choice but to buy wine and meat for him. Seeing that they feared him, Li Kui began talking still more wildly. Everyone in the prison grew more frightened still. They brought hot water for him to bathe and gave him clean clothes to change into. Li Kui said, “If ever I am short of wine or food, I will fly away and leave you to suffer for it.” The prison guards could only humble themselves and beg his indulgence. For the present, we leave Li Kui confined in the Jizhou prison.

p.src: Now Perfected Man Luo related all the foregoing events to Dai Zong, one by one. Dai Zong pleaded with him most earnestly to save Li Kui. Perfected Man Luo kept Dai Zong overnight at the abbey and asked about affairs at the mountain stronghold. Dai Zong told him of the many virtues of Heavenly King Chao and Song Gongming: how they upheld justice and freely shared their wealth, devoted themselves solely to carrying out Heaven's will, and had sworn never to harm loyal ministers or valiant men, filial sons or worthy descendants, righteous husbands or chaste wives. Perfected Man Luo was greatly pleased when he had heard him out. Dai Zong remained there five days, kowtowing and making obeisance every day as he implored the Perfected Man to save Li Kui. Perfected Man Luo said, “A man like that ought simply to be done away with. You had better not take him back.” Dai Zong pleaded, “You do not know, Perfected Man. Though Li Kui is foolish and ignorant of reason and propriety, he does have some small virtues. First, he is forthright and honest, and would never improperly take so much as a fraction from another man; second, he never flatters or fawns upon anyone, and even in the face of death his loyalty remains unchanged; third, he is utterly free of lustful or wicked thoughts, never covets wealth or betrays righteousness, and always charges bravely to the fore. For these reasons Song Gongming is very fond of him. If I were to go back without him, how could this humble one face my elder brother Song Gongming?” Perfected Man Luo laughed. “I already know that this man is the incarnation ordained for the Star of Heavenly Slaughter in the upper realm. Because the beings of this earthly realm have amassed too much evil karma, he was sentenced to descend and carry out slaughter. How could I defy Heaven and destroy him? I merely wished to discipline him for a while. I shall have him fetched and returned to you.” Dai Zong bowed in gratitude.
